newsitem.title: USA: Texas Star resumes Diamonds crater tests.
newsitem.headline: Texas Star resumes Diamonds crater tests.

text.p: Texas Star Resources said on Friday that it resumed testing at a crater in Arkansas's Diamonds State Park, after a U.S. judge lifted a temporary restraining order against the company.

The environmental group, Friends of the Crater of Diamonds, had filed for a restraining order against the exploration company. But a judge denied their request for a temporary and permanent injuction and a judgement was issued in favor of continued testing in the park, Texas Star said.
Costs were assessed to the plaintiffs, Texas Star quoted the judgement as saying.

Texas Star said it was one of two participants qualified with the State of Arkansas to assist in testing the lamproite pipe at the park. The company said the lifting of restraining order allowed the trenching of test material to resume.
Three of the scheduled 14- mini-trenches have already been excavated and reclaimed, it said.
Processing of additional mini-trenches would continue and should be completed in the next 90 to 120 days, it said.
